title: Park the already painted instance of the selected native System in a close-world round trip

scope.subject: Retain the same pinned System renderer resources across the close-world detour, park presentation and update work, and keep exact camera handoffs.

research_summary: Exact main 8d394498 CI 45842755667 timed out on LOW repeated return with requested System 1.000 but only a few paints. Original exact local test passes naturally; matching cadence fails with fresh target 1 and positive clamp. Exact local first-use driver APIs block up to 1.1s outbound; current Surface terrain hidden and not drawing. Pinned Three r185 on SwiftShader has no KHR_parallel_shader_compile and a real WebGL shadow finds compileAsync resolves before remaining first-draw blocking. Hiding retains five shader variants, submits no draws and reactivates with existing materials. Existing Surface retained lifecycle is the model, not a parallel camera/cache.

sources.finding: Keep this pinned native BodyRenderer, BodyPoints and OrbitLines under the existing R3F Canvas owner.
Product already retains a hidden owner and gates visibility synchronously with phaseRef at frame priority -100; updates explicitly stop while parked.
Installed Three renderer skips invisible subtrees including their lights; preserving geometry/material references retains their program keys until bounded owner disposal.
R3F subscribers share the original renderer and execute in priority order; existing project draws at priority 1 and publishes post-draw evidence at priority 2.
Installed compileAsync depends on KHR_parallel_shader_compile for actual readiness, missing on the exact local SwiftShader; shadow found first-use stalls after promise.

search_ladder.conclusion: Preserve the pinned YEIS backbone, not a new renderer or camera.
Retain one owner in the existing Canvas; do not add alternate render loop or scene cache.
Reuse the existing Surface lifetime pattern and synchronous presentation fence; keep only one already drawn same identity instance.
Reuse TypeScript lifecycles and Three visible flag; await compileAsync does not guarantee SwiftShader first-use reflection readiness.

candidates.name: Park the same native scene as existing Surface owner
candidates.reason: Preserves same renderer, camera, materials and product authority; hides parked native updates and releases on identity or phase exit.

candidates.name: Keep alive with Three group visibility
candidates.reason: Useful primitive; does not guard update or scale publications on its own.

candidates.name: Pre-warm with compileAsync
candidates.reason: No KHR extension on the verified SwiftShader; matched shadow still blocks after its promise, and it does not preserve native scene program lifetime.

decision.rationale: Keep the same already published render owner, explicitly cease all native work when hidden, dispose on identity/quality/context/unmount and keep genuine matched camera fences, shader validation, timing and resource guards unchanged.
decision.fallback: Keep baseline if identity, dwell, paint, shader timing or resource evidence fails; do not waive the original LOW assertion.
